episodes.169946: An isolated severe thunderstorm produced some wind damage.
episodes.170018: According to broadcast media reports, a lightning strike caused one fatality and multiple injuries at Fort Gordon, GA.
episodes.170067: Moisture values continued to be on the rise across northern and central New Mexico on July 20, 2022, and this led to a very active monsoon day for the area. Scattered to numerous thunderstorms were common across much of the area, particularly across the mountainous terrain. New Mexico's recent burn scars continued to  be magnets for heavy thunderstorms with known impacts across the McBride burn scar as well as the Hermits Peak and Calf Canyon burn scar. Meanwhile, thunderstorms also produced brief strong winds in a couple locations.
episodes.170079: High-based showers and thunderstorms developed into northwestern Arkansas during the early morning hours of the 20th. The strongest storm produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.170343: A surface cold front moved southeastward from southeastern Lower Michigan and far-northwest Ohio to central Lake Erie and north-central and southwestern portions of Ohio during the evening of the 20th. Bands of organized thunderstorms, mainly in the form of multicells, occurred along and especially ahead of the front. These storms encountered a warm sector comprised of moderate to strong effective bulk shear and MUCAPE, respectively, and strong DCAPE. This environment allowed sporadic convective straight-line wind damage to occur. A supercell embedded within the pre-frontal squall line generated a brief tornado in far-southern Wayne and far-northern Holmes Counties as the supercell encountered favorably-low mixed layer LCL's and large surface-based effective SRH.
episodes.170367: A surface cold front moved southeastward from Lake Michigan and northeastern Illinois to southeastern Lower Michigan and far-northwest Ohio during the late morning through early evening of the 20th. This allowed Lake Erie to remain within the warm sector. Multicell showers and thunderstorms produced isolated gale-force to storm-force peak gusts along the Ohio shore of western Lake Erie as they encountered moderate to strong MUCAPE, DCAPE, and effective bulk shear, respectively.
episodes.170777: Strong thunderstorms associated with the sea breeze collision moved eastward through Volusia and Brevard counties, producing a brief water spout on the beach in Daytona Beach Shores, and strong wind gusts along the coast and intracoastal waters near Daytona Beach, Lagrange, Kennedy Space Center.
episodes.171524: A cold front tracking through southeast Michigan during the afternoon hours of July 20, 2022 led to widespread thunderstorm development and severe weather reports across the area. The main threat with these storms was damaging winds, as the line of storms moved through between 1-4 PM. Several reports of trees and powerlines down as well as a 66 mph wind gust at Detroit Metro Airport were recorded. A second round of storms developed between 4-6 PM as the cold front cleared the area, primarily impacting the extreme eastern portions of the CWA near the Lake Huron shoreline.
episodes.171734: A seasonably impressive cyclone and associated upper-level shortwave quickly progressed over the upper Great Lakes on 7/20, providing support for thunderstorms to develop over northern Michigan during the early afternoon along an advancing cold front. These storms eventually moved over portions of Lake Huron, producing wind gusts in excess of 40 mph over the nearshore waters.
episodes.171809: A line of thunderstorms developed in the late morning hours across portions of central Georgia and the Midlands of South Carolina. These thunderstorms progressed into interior portions of southeast South Carolina and produced damaging wind gusts in the early afternoon.
episodes.171811: Clusters of thunderstorms developed inland across southeast Georgia and gradually shifted to the coast in the afternoon. These thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts along the southeast Georgia coast.
episodes.171839: Steering flow WSW steering flow and lingering high moisture across NE FL brought a more dominant west coast sea breeze regime with storms moving west to east across FL through the day. Pulse severe storms produced wet downbursts and locally heavy rainfall.
episodes.171903: It was a fairly typical summer-time regime in place with abundant moisture available and warm temperatures expected. Convergence along sea-breeze boundaries sparked off thunderstorm development. It was along these boundaries that a thunderstorm produced severe gusts in marine Lake Borne.
episodes.171904: It was a fairly typical summer-time regime in place with abundant moisture available and warm temperatures expected. Convergence along sea-breeze boundaries sparked off thunderstorm development. It was along these boundaries that a thunderstorm produced severe gusts in marine areas. That same storm grew westward from Lake Borne across the city of New Orleans. In doing so, movement was slow and thus flash flooding occurred.
episodes.172066: Thunderstorms moving through Saginaw Bay and southern Lake Huron produced winds near 50 knots.
episodes.172067: A thunderstorm moving through Lake St. Clair produced a wind gust just under 35 knots.
episodes.172068: A thunderstorm moving through western Lake Erie produced a wind gust in excess of 40 knots.
episodes.172240: Thunderstorms passed through the southern James River Valley, with one storm producing nickel size hail in Dickey County.
episodes.172246: Another upper level disturbance rotated south through the region on the afternoon of July 20, igniting thunderstorms in several locations. Excessively hot conditions provided more than adequate instability for the production of severe downburst winds with several of these storms.
episodes.172285: Showers and thunderstorms occurred over and near the higher terrain as well as into the I-25 corridor during the afternoon and evening. An isolated wind gust to 58 mph occurred across southern El Paso county, along with a localized heavy rainfall report near the Wet Mountains.
episodes.172432: A pre-frontal trough was present across western North Carolina amid a warm and moist airmass. A cold front moved southeast into the northern Mid-Atlantic, Ohio Valley, and the mid-south toward the morning of the 21st. Ahead of these surface boundaries, scattered showers and storms developed over southern North Carolina in the evening, from the southern Piedmont, eastward across the Sandhills and southern Coastal Plain. Some of the storms over Stanly and Moore Counties produced tree and power line damage.
episodes.172460: Enough moisture lingered for thunderstorms to produce flash flooding just south of the Mogollon Rim in Gila County.
episodes.172493: A typical summertime pattern prevailed with scattered afternoon thunderstorms across the tri-state region.  A few reports of wind damage occurred across northwest Florida.
episodes.172503: Monsoon moisture surged back across northern Arizona which allowed strong to severe thunderstorms to form.
episodes.172506: Scattered strong summer storms resulted in gusty winds in excess of 34 knots as well across portions of the coastal waters.
episodes.172548: Above average temperatures within a dry airmass developed throughout the day. As a result of reaching convective temperatures, high based thunderstorms developed due to the dry airmass. One thunderstorm created a severe wind gust of 60 mph that was reported at the Texline mesonet station.
episodes.172627: Another active setup in mid-late July resulted in numerous microburst related wind gusts in portions of Utah's West Desert Region, as well as a report of severe hail. Additionally, flash flooding was noted in southern Utah. This also coincided with a period of anomalous heat across much of the region.
episodes.172672: After the two months of dry and sunny weather due to mostly upper level ridging in place across much of Alaska, the pattern flipped for the second half of the month to more of an upper level trough as the upper level ridge shifted to the east. This resulted in multiple storm systems moving into Southcentral with rounds of heavy rainfall that resulted in small streams and river rises in the area.
episodes.172681: Scattered thunderstorms moved southwest off the Mogollon Rim then turned west and became severe across Cochise and Santa Cruz counties during the late afternoon and evening. A microburst caused extensive damage to homes north of Douglas and severe wind gusts occurred farther west from Sierra Vista to Nogales.
episodes.172787: A humid airmass remained in place beneath a west-northwesterly flow aloft. Weak boundaries triggered convection in WNW to ESE oriented bands, some which were anchored to higher terrain. The result was excessive rainfall with training cells.
episodes.172791: A thunderstorm anchored and redeveloping over higher terrain near Marble NC produced up to 8 inches of rain.
episodes.172845: Wind and hail damage was reported across portions of Sargent County during the evening hours as an isolated severe thunderstorm impacted the area.
episodes.172943: Scattered thunderstorms and storm clusters developed over western North Carolina during the afternoon and evening. A couple of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts. Slow-moving storm cells also produced locally excessive rainfall in Union County.
episodes.172945: Scattered thunderstorms developed over the North Carolina foothills during the afternoon. One of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts in Rutherford County.
episodes.172973: Isolated gale-force wind gusts occurred with scattered showers and thunderstorms embedded in a fresh easterly lower tropospheric flow.
episodes.173069: Multiple waves of typical daytime summertime showers and thunderstorms developed within a modestly unstable and abnormally moist tropical airmass during the afternoon and evenings of July 19th through July 21st.  These storms produced numerous reports of trees and powerlines down, quarter size hail, and flash flooding across portions of north and central Georgia.
